script.base: Book expects BAL to lead (implied 29.5 to MIA 22.0) in a 51.5 game, not a slog. Base flow: BAL ahead by halftime or late and closes with Derrick Henry, who has 60 carries / 226 yards in weeks 5/6/8 (~20 carries, 3.77 YPC). MIA as a +7.5 dog throws more once behind; Waddle (18 tgt / 209 yds / 282 air), Washington (18/88/60) and Achane (18 tgt, plus 47 car / 277 rush) are the outlets. Leader-runs-late is the base, not an automatic blowout at 7.5.
script.flip1: MIA hangs around or leads. BAL has allowed 26 passes of 20+ and 8.27 YPA in the middle (56 att). A shootout or dog-lead script stalls Henry in the 33- and 42-yard range from his last four and lifts MIA explosives (Waddle last4 110/95/15/99) instead of the BAL clock-grind.
script.flip2: BAL blows it open early. Henry's carries jump then Tyler Huntley (11/92 in the same three-game window) or Keaton Mitchell (7/51) vultures the explosives and late snaps get cut. MIA abandons the run, so Achane's 64.5 rush line dies (he already has a 16-yard rush game) while garbage-time throws prop up short targets.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and Henry under 50.5 lost the ticket. BAL did not lead: MIA hit the middle-of-field bleed (8.27 YPA) and the 26-explosive pass profile, so the offense passed and Henry finished in the 33-42 band already on his last4 card. Or BAL led big and Huntley (11 carries, 92 yards, 8.4 YPC in the only recent window) and Mitchell took the explosive runs while Henry was pulled short of 50.5. A second path: the 5.21 YPC allowed is real but Henry's own 3.77 YPC traveled, the unknown outdoor forecast cut play volume, or a QB/carry-share change the injury report does not document showed up at inactives. The counter-case is strong enough to keep this a lean, not a strong, and to refuse a second leg that needs the opposite script.
